Born: October 20, 1964, 9:28 PM local time, Oakland, California, USA. Source: Astro-Databank, Rodden rating AA.

The AA rating means the time comes from a birth certificate or birth record, so the rising sign, the Midheaven and the houses below can be taken at face value. Open Kamala Harris's chart on Astrolas alongside this read.

One feature anchors the whole chart. Three planets sit together in Virgo, in the 4th house, the part of the chart the Astrolas library ties to home, family and the ground a life gets built on. The IC, the floor of that same house, falls in Virgo too.

Harris became the 49th Vice President of the United States in 2021, the first woman and the first Black and South Asian American to hold the office, after serving as a US Senator from California and, before that, as the state's Attorney General. Her mother, Shyamala Gopalan, came from India to study nutrition science and went on to become a breast cancer researcher. Her father, Donald Harris, came from Jamaica to study economics. A chart built around the 4th house fits a public life that keeps returning to where she came from.

muc.ten: Venus, Uranus and Pluto together in Virgo, in the 4th house
doan: Venus sits at 17°54', Uranus at 13°15' and Pluto at 15°27', all Virgo, all in the 4th house, with the IC at 2°24' Virgo underneath them.

The library's Virgo texts read as a family built on care and improvement. Venus in Virgo is selective and cautious in love, reserved until it trusts, then sincere and devoted. Uranus in Virgo brings reform through sharp analysis and a steady search for a better method; at the generational level it marks a whole cohort reshaping its relationship to work and health. Pluto in Virgo is a generational marker too, tied to the years 1957 to 1971, when civil rights and feminist movements reshaped public life, a backdrop that lines up with Harris's own path into law.

The 4th-house texts turn those signs toward home directly. Venus in the 4th decorates a home with quiet taste rather than display, and stays close to family in a gentle, steady way. Uranus in the 4th describes a family life that does not fit the conventional mold, often because a parent differs from the people around them in interests, career or background, which fits a household built by two immigrant academics from different continents. Pluto in the 4th ties a strong inner drive to the home itself, often shaped by a demanding parent, with privacy held tightly within the family.

Two aspects connect this group directly. Uranus conjunct Pluto, orb 2°12', is a generational aspect, last exact in the 1960s, read by the library as independence and a rebellious, renewing spirit that tends to erupt hardest in midlife. Venus conjunct Pluto, orb 2°26', brings magnetism with an edge of intensity, along with strong artistic and financial ability, and a caution about possessiveness.

muc.ten: Moon in Aries, in the 11th house
doan: The Moon sits at 27°39' Aries, in the 11th house of friends, groups and causes. The library reads this Moon as bold and assertive, hating constraint, and notes directly that a life like this is often marked by sudden turns toward power, especially in politics. Its 11th-house placement treats close friends as family and often puts a person in a leadership role inside clubs, organizations or movements, with goals that shift as the mood does but rarely lose their underlying drive.

That combination, an assertive Moon inside a house built on groups and causes, fits a career that moved through student government at Howard University, a district attorney's office, and eventually national politics, each step built on organizing people around a shared goal.

muc.ten: Sun in Libra and Mercury in Scorpio, both in the 5th house
doan: The Sun sits at 27°48' Libra and Mercury at 1°28' Scorpio, both in the 5th house. Libra Sun brings diplomacy, fairness and the instinct to see every side of an argument, with the 5th-house placement adding a love of performance and a strong identification with personal creative projects. Scorpio Mercury digs beneath the surface of every question and is drawn to work that rewards that instinct: research, investigation, law.

The Sun and Moon oppose each other almost exactly, orb 0°10', the tightest aspect anywhere in this chart, though the library has no text for it yet. Read only as structure, it places the fair-minded, sociable Libra Sun directly across from the bold, self-driven Aries Moon, a built-in tension between weighing every side and acting on instinct. The Sun also trines Saturn, orb 0°39', and the Moon sextiles Saturn, orb 0°49', two more tight, textless links that tie both luminaries to the disciplined Saturn covered next.

muc.ten: Saturn in Aquarius, in the 9th house
doan: Saturn sits at 28°28' Aquarius, retrograde, in the 9th house of law, higher education and belief. The library reads Saturn in Aquarius as discipline fused with humanitarian, forward-looking thinking, naming politics and society directly as fields where the combination succeeds, alongside law. Its 9th-house placement, read here as retrograde, ties success in higher education to a slower, more inward process, with legal matters and personal belief systems revisited and re-earned rather than handed over easily.

Harris earned her law degree at UC Hastings College of Law after Howard University, then built a legal career that ran from local prosecutor to the state's top law enforcement officer. The library's read on a 9th-house Saturn, success through education that comes later but holds firm, fits that long, procedural route into public life.

muc.ten: Mars in Leo, in the 3rd house
doan: Mars sits at 21°18' Leo, in the 3rd house of communication and everyday argument. The library's Leo Mars wants to assert itself and draw attention, with a gift for public speaking and leadership, provided the drive to be the center does not tip into domineering. Its 3rd-house placement is read here as outspoken and fervent, always wanting to steer a conversation, with quick reactions and a proactive spirit, alongside a caution about impulsiveness in debate.
That is a fair description of a career built partly on courtroom argument and televised questioning, first as a prosecutor and later in Senate hearings.

muc.ten: Jupiter in Taurus, in the 12th house
doan: Jupiter sits at 24°00' Taurus, retrograde, in the 12th house of what stays private. The library reads Jupiter in Taurus as a talent for building and holding material stability, often through finance or real estate, paired with a genuine appreciation for beauty and comfort. Its 12th-house placement, retrograde here, describes protection and generosity that arrive quietly rather than visibly, with a tendency to give behind the scenes and a need to trust one's own intuition rather than always waiting for help to show itself.

muc.ten: Gemini rising, and the angles without library text yet
doan: The Ascendant sits at 24°25' Gemini, with the Descendant at 24°25' Sagittarius, the Midheaven at 2°24' Pisces and the IC at 2°24' Virgo, already covered above as the floor of the 4th-house group. The Astrolas library does not yet have entries for the Ascendant or the Midheaven on their own. Mercury trines the Midheaven almost exactly, orb 0°57', and Venus sextiles Neptune, orb 1°04', two more tight aspects the library has not written up yet, so this article notes them only as structure.

muc.ten: What the chart adds up to
doan: The chart does not explain how someone becomes a Vice President. What it lines up with is a life that kept building outward from a tightly held foundation: three planets anchoring Virgo in the 4th house, a Moon in the 11th that turns friendship into a political base, and a Saturn in the 9th that pays out slowly through law and education.
